summary.text: This opportunity briefing explores combining Gaussian processes, principal component analysis, and uncertainty quantification to handle high-dimensional or infinite-dimensional transient responses. Specifically, functional principal component analysis reduces the dimension of time-dependent profiles while preserving their structural characteristics. Gaussian processes and surrogate models are subsequently trained on these principal component scores to facilitate efficient sampling and uncertainty propagation.

target_user.text: The target user is unverified due to a lack of patent assignee data, but packages and repositories in the bundle suggest users include practitioners working with modular machine learning libraries, uncertainty baselines, and geometric kernels.

jtbd.text: Perform Bayesian inverse uncertainty quantification with time-dependent or transient experimental data by compressing high-dimensional responses into lower-dimensional scores.

value_prop.text: It overcomes the computational bottlenecks of high-dimensional responses in inverse uncertainty quantification by leveraging functional principal component analysis for dimensionality reduction and Gaussian processes for probabilistic surrogate modeling.
